question: Why does the growth of an onion root stop after its tip is cut?

options.text: The apical meristem that produces new cells is removed.
The meristematic cells lose their vacuoles.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The apical meristem that produces new cells is removed.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **apical meristem** is a group of actively dividing cells located at the tips of roots and shoots. It is responsible for the primary growth of plants, including elongation of the root. When the tip of the root is cut, this meristematic region is removed, halting further elongation. ***Hence, this statement is correct.***
 
• **Intercalary meristem**, on the other hand, is found in specific regions such as the base of leaves or internodes in grasses and does not contribute to root elongation. Its role is unrelated to the growth of the root tip. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
